name: fallback
algorithm: Per round, splitmix64 gives r; a list of (r & 63) + 1 u64 values r + i, or of (r & 1023) + 1 when the top four bits of r are zero, is built with the standard growable list in an allocator that serves from a 1 KiB stack buffer and falls back to the general-purpose allocator, summed and released; the checksum is the wrapping sum over rounds (../README.md).

skip.c: no allocator with a stack buffer and a fallback in the C standard library
skip.rust: no allocator with a stack buffer and a fallback in Rust's standard library (the Allocator API is unstable)
skip.go: no allocator with a stack buffer and a fallback in Go's standard library

notes: Mk: std.mem.Fallback over a 1 KiB stack buffer, then std's general heap, and HeapList[u64]; Zig: std.heap.BufferFirstAllocator over a 1 KiB stack buffer, then std.heap.smp_allocator, and std.ArrayList(u64). The lists grow differently (Mk max(4, 2 cap), Zig cap + cap/2 + 8), so a list leaves the buffer at a different length in each: Mk's holds 128 values in the buffer.
